superseded_record_text.notes: This is the ruby-pressure assignment of the same 16-row compression/decompression experiment represented by the companion ice-VII-scale record. It is a distinct fit, not a duplicate parameter transcription. The paper reports that V0 was varied and stayed within 0.01% of the measured in-cell value, while K0 was fixed at the adopted 212 GPa Brillouin value. Ruby-line broadening above 15 GPa showed increasing nonhydrostatic stress; the authors therefore regarded K0'=7.5 as less realistic than the ice-VII-scale result. The source gives neither parameter covariance nor a confidence convention for parenthesized fit errors, and it does not specify an exact ruby calibration equation. The numerical 298 K reference encodes the source's qualitative 'ambient temperature' wording rather than a measured sample temperature.

Ice-VII (110) diffraction and MgSiO3 ilmenite were measured on the same 50 micrometer X-ray spot; Table 1 prints 12 finite-pressure Pi values, and Figure 3f additionally plots the two ambient measurements as zero-pressure anchors, giving 14 usable rows. The paper reports that V0 was varied and K0 was fixed at the adopted 212 GPa Brillouin value. Above 15 GPa the pressure medium developed nonhydrostatic stress and pressure gradients; the bracketed ice-pressure quantities are maximum gradient estimates, not stated one-sigma errors. The source gives neither parameter covariance nor a confidence convention for fitted-parameter errors. The numerical 298 K reference encodes the source's qualitative 'ambient temperature' wording rather than a measured sample temperature.
